Abstract
Gated attention is an efective approach to mitigate attention
sinks and enhance the representational capacity of attention.
To further extend its efectiveness-eficiency Pareto frontier,
we propose a Hybrid Gated Attention (HyGA) framework that
contains three types of gating strategies. Specifically, these
gates leverage diverse information from multiple stages of
attention, and collaboratively build element-wise/head-wise
gating from multiple perspectives, capturing intra-head and
cross-head information interactions. Through our hybrid gat-
ing components, HyGA could provide multi-source modula-
tion signals, enabling more comprehensive control over infor-
mation flow and improving the representational capacity of
attention. We also introduce low-rank matrix decomposition
and learnable attention sink to further enhance training efi-
ciency and stability. In experiments, we evaluate HyGA on
widely-used benchmarks based on diferent backbones. The
experimental results show that our HyGA comprehensively
improves both training loss and various downstream perfor-
mances compared with Gated attention. HyGA has also been
verified to achieve the best performance at diferent compu-
tation costs, with comprehensive model analyses for better
understanding. The proposed HyGA sheds light on a more
efective, eficient, and stable attention mechanism.

hance nonlinear modulation. This is because the above form

stable information flow and stronger expressive capacity.

While pursuing improved model expressiveness, we also at-
tempt to minimize the computation cost to extend the Pareto
frontier between efectiveness and eficiency. Although the
two gate mechanisms described above could cooperate well,
there may still exist partial functional overlap between them,
enabling them to withstand greater information compression.
Therefore, we can use low-rank factorization to reduce com-
putation and parameter cost while preserving most of the
expressive capacity.

5 Related Works
Gating Method in Neural Networks Gating is a long-
standing method for controlling information flow in neu-
ral networks. Early models such as LSTMs (Hochreiter and
Schmidhuber 1997) and GRUs(Cho et al. 2014) use gates to
regulate memory updates, while later works such as GLU
(Dauphin et al. 2017)and SwiGLU (Shazeer 2020) further
introduce gating into feed-forward activations. Gating also
plays an important role in modern recurrent and state-space

models, including S4, Mamba, and Mamba-2 (Gu, Goel, and
Ré 2021; Gu and Dao 2023; Dao and Gu 2024), where it
controls state updates and memory retention. These exam-
ples suggest that gating is not merely an auxiliary technique,
but a general architectural principle for improving selectivity
and expressive capacity.
Gated Attention and Its Variants Gated attention (Qiu
et al. 2026b) introduces a head-specific sigmoid gate after
the scaled dot-product attention output, showing that this
simple modification improves performance and training sta-
bility. This work provides the foundation for studying gating
as a structural enhancement to attention rather than as a pe-
ripheral fusion module. Since Gated attention, some related
studies have explored several directions related to gated at-
tention. Some works place gates at diferent locations in the
attention computation, such as applying a forget gate to un-
normalized attention scores (Lin et al. 2025) or computing
gates from value states to mitigate extreme-token phenom-
ena (Bu et al. 2025). Another significant direction is low-rank
gate, such as gated norm (Qiu et al. 2026a). While these stud-
ies demonstrate the usefulness and generality of gating, they
typically investigate individual design dimensions, such as
gate placement or low-rank parameterization. In contrast, our
work focuses on the architecture of the gate itself by jointly
considering its conditioning pathways, coupling mechanism,
parameterization, and cross-head interaction, aiming to im-
prove the model performance and training stability.
6 Conclusion and Future Work
In this work, we introduced HyGA with three gates depend
on diferent inputs and granularities: X-gate, H-gate, and
C-gate. Besides, we also adopt low-rank matrix decomposi-
tion and learnable sink for eficiency and training stability.
Through more comprehensive information interaction capa-
bility, HyGA achieves improved performance.
In the future, we plan to scale HyGA to larger models
and evaluate its efectiveness at greater scales. We will also
investigate its generalizability across diferent attention back-
bones, such as linear/sparse attention architectures.
